differences.what: massing: the long north flank, the round tower close behind the front, the two very tall stacks and the front block's steep street hip stand where the plate draws them, the stacks' tops and the tower's top within about 10-25 px through this view's camera (fitted to them, the hip's apex and the front's north eave)
the street hip's pitch: the plate's front hip rises to its finial at about 15.9 m, 6.4 m over the 9.5 m eave; built at 52 degrees (T-3280), where T-3279 had 45

the round tower's top: the plate carries the tower past its third tier of windows as a plain band to a flat top with a heavy edge; built as a fourth, windowless 1.9 m storey under K08's nearly flat tin cap (T-3280), where T-3279 had a slated cone and finial
the broad street dormer of three lights under its gable: built 3.3 m wide with three lights (T-3280)

where the broad dormer stands along the front: through this camera its face lies about 1.6 m south of the front's centre, where the 2004 photograph shows it about 1 m north of it; built on the centre, between the two readings

the smaller one-light street dormer near the front's south end, under its own steep gable, and the stack rising behind the street dormers at the front block's south side: T-3301 built the dormer 1.6 m wide at v 8.05 m with one light (K01's `dormer.also`) and the stack at u 14.5 m, v 7.5 m; through this camera the small dormer stands beside the broad one where the plate draws it, and the stack rises behind the broad dormer's gable within about 1 m of the plate's, just north of where the plate draws it at the gable's south slope

the broad dormer's stone-coped gable with kneelers and finial: T-3301 built a stone coping along each rake over the slate, a kneeler block at each foot and a small turned finial at the apex (K01's `dormer.coping`), the small dormer coped the same way; the plate's gable reads a little steeper than the built 45 degrees (about 0.5 m higher at the apex), which the 2004 photograph does not bear out, so it stays

the small pinnacled dormers between the gables: all three plates draw two over the flank's flat-topped bays, below and left of the big gable. With the rear range ridged across (T-3354), its north slope faces this camera between the street gable and the far gables, and the two dormers stand at its foot, about over the rear range's north-east corner and the middle range's north end (through the 1919 programme plate's camera their tops fall at about u -9, v -3.6 on that slope and over the middle range's flank gable). Not built: K01 lays no dormer on a wing's slope, and where the middle range's flank gable stands the plates draw these dormers and no gable (below)

the north flank's two-storey bays with flat tops and their stone mullioned windows: T-3337 builds the 1911 sheet's canted north bay on the rear range (u -14.5 to -9.4, 1.2 m out where the sheet reads about 1.4), two storeys to the range's wall top, flat-topped under a moulded stone cornice and a stone balustrade, with a four-light stone-mullioned transomed group on its face in each storey and a sash in each cheek, the range's gable standing back over it; the quoined block at the middle range's north-west corner and its mullioned stretch are not built

stone belts and dressings on the front block: the plate shows pale stone courses across the brick and a pale basement; T-3305 lays the basement to the principal floor under the front, the bow, the tower and the north flank, and three stone courses on the front carried round the main block's north flank (under the principal sills, at the second floor, under the chamber sills) in place of K03's brick string course. Through this camera the main block's flank stands mostly behind the lamp and the ivy, so the courses' lines there are judged by eye against the pale bands the plate shows on the front block, not measured; the plainest stone in the plate, on the rear ranges' bays, is the next item's

the main cornice over the front's north part: the plate runs the eave level across the front and round onto the flank over the trees, with no break where the bow stands below; T-3313 carries the bow up to the eave and the cornice's bed moulding, soffit and fascia round it, where T-3279's bow stopped under the bed with its own low cap
the front's lower storeys, its bow and the stoop: the parkway trees hide them
colour: the plate is monochrome
the electric street lamp, the automobile, the parkway trees and the fence's pattern: not part of this record

the rear ranges' stone: the plate draws pale quoins up the corners of the north flank's stepped-out ranges and pale courses across them, plainest of all its walls; T-3353 quoins both ranges' north-east corners (where each range's north wall meets the face it steps out on), long and short stones in turn from grade to the wall top, and carries the main block's three stone courses (under the principal sills, at the second floor, under the chamber sills) across both ranges' north walls and stepped-out faces in place of K03's brick course; through this camera the pale corners and bands stand where the plate's do, the stones themselves too fine in the halftone to count

the rear range's canted north bay's own corners: the plate draws the bay dark (brick or ivy) between the range's pale corners and does not resolve its own; T-3354 read it again in the 1912 Blue Book plate, whose coarser halftone draws it in deep shade among the trees and resolves no corner either, and the 1913 plate sees it under trees. No plate shows whether its corners are quoined, so it is built in brick with its stone-mullioned groups (T-3337) and no quoins of its own

the big gable over the rear range (T-3354): read as a gable facing the street, not the flank. These cameras see the flank at about 60 degrees, so a 50-degree flank gable draws about 70 degrees steep, where the plates draw its rakes at about 45 and its face lit as the street front is; and the old flank gable stood 20-35 px left of the plates' apex. The rear range is now ridged across (gabled to the street and the rear) at 16.6 m on 58 degrees, its street gable standing over the middle range's wall top, coped, kneelered and finialled; through this camera its apex lands on the plate's within about 10 px (the finial's top on the plate's peak)

the rear range's ridge running back west from the street gable: the shallow line the plates draw from the big apex to a small peak is that ridge, and its west end (the range's coped rear gable at u -16.4) lands about 33 px right of the plate's peak here and 26 px in the 1913 Almanac plate (one viewpoint, one fit), but on the 1912 Blue Book plate's peak within about 10 px: the plates disagree by about 2-3 m along the line of sight

the middle range's own gable, kept facing the flank (apex 13.8 m, T-3337): it now stands in front of the street gable's foot, where the plates draw the two pinnacled dormers over the flat-topped bays and no gable of their own; not rebuilt here, its roof waiting on how the dormers stand on it

the third, smaller gable the plates draw at the flank's far end, coped and finialled as the ranges' are: T-3354 roofs the garage under a slated gable facing the flank, pitched 54 degrees to an apex at 15.7 m, with the ranges' stone coping, kneelers and 0.6 m finial (where it was flat in tin); through this camera its apex lands on the plate's third gable within about 15 px

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
